short: FILTER (WHERE ...) after an aggregate: that one aggregate only sees the rows where the condition holds.
turning rows into columns: one filtered aggregate per output column, grouped by the row key. the columns must be known when the query is written.
several GROUP BYs in one query, their results stacked. a column a set doesn't group by comes out NULL.
ROLLUP (a, b) is the grouping sets (a, b), (a) and (): detail rows, a subtotal per a, a grand total.
CUBE (a, b) is every subset of its columns as a grouping set: (a, b), (a), (b) and ().
1 when its column was rolled up in this row's grouping set, 0 when it was grouped. tells a subtotal's NULL from a real one.
an aggregate that needs its input sorted, given in WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...): percentile_cont, percentile_disc, mode.
the value at a fraction of the sorted input, interpolated between neighbours. percentile_cont(0.5) is the median.
the first real value at or past a fraction of the sorted input. never interpolates, so it works on any sortable type.
where a value would land if it were in the group: rank(88000) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary DESC).
the group of rows a window function works within, set by PARTITION BY. no PARTITION BY means one partition: every row.
names a window once (WINDOW w AS (...)) so several window functions can share it with OVER w.
the slice of the partition a window function reads for the current row. ROWS counts rows, RANGE measures values, GROUPS counts peer groups.
a row that ties with the current row on the window's ORDER BY. RANGE and GROUPS frames take peers as a block.
EXCLUDE CURRENT ROW, GROUP or TIES: takes rows back out of a frame after the bounds have chosen it.
row_number numbers rows uniquely, rank ties and skips, dense_rank ties without skipping. they only differ on ties.
lag(x, n, default): x from n rows before the current one in the window's order. LEAD looks ahead.
a sum of every row so far: sum(x) OVER (ORDER BY ...), which uses the default frame.
the best n rows of every group: row_number in a subquery, a LATERAL ... LIMIT n per group, or DISTINCT ON for n = 1.
finding runs of consecutive values (islands) and the holes between them. value minus row_number is constant inside a run.
WITH RECURSIVE: an anchor, UNION ALL, and a part that refers to the CTE itself, repeated until it finds no new rows.
in a recursive CTE, the rows the previous round found. the next round joins against these only; an empty one stops the loop.
recursive CTE clauses: SEARCH sets a depth-first or breadth-first sort column, CYCLE marks and stops a loop. postgres 14+.
a row for every date in a range, from generate_series, LEFT JOINed to the data so empty days still get a row.
a function that returns rows instead of one value, like generate_series or unnest. in FROM it can see tables to its left.
